title: How to organise the power tool storage | Workshop
description:
Keep every corded and cordless tool guarded, complete with its own accessories, and ready to pick up and use.

This is the Power Tool Storage in the Workshop. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Each tool in a labeled home with its guard closed and its blade wrench or chuck key attached to it, not floating in a drawer. Batteries sitting on a shelf off the chargers, no bare circular saw blade loose in a drawer, and no cord repaired with electrical tape anywhere in the zone.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Line up the duplicates and be honest about the second drill and the sander you replaced but kept.
Straighten: Store each tool with the parts that make it usable: the circular saw with its rip fence and blade wrench, the
Shine: Blow or brush the motor vents clear of packed sawdust, take the pitch off saw blades with resin remover so the
Safety: Work the retracting guard on every saw with your thumb and confirm it snaps back on its own; a sticky guard is
Standardize: Label each tool's home on the wall or the shelf edge, and set one charge rule for the batteries: partial charg
Sustain: When a battery goes onto the charger at the end of a job, the tool it came off goes onto its hook in the same

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Every tool rests guarded, unplugged, and stored with the accessories it needs to work.
